core_obligations: Tensor the given short exact sequence of complexes with an arbitrary complex L and obtain a short exact sequence of total complexes (proof lines 14263-14270).
Verify degreewise exactness of that sequence using the flatness hypothesis and the vanishing of Tor (proof lines 14270-14278).
Apply the two-out-of-three property for acyclicity of complexes to conclude that K-flatness also satisfies two out of three (proof lines 14278-14281).
proof_roadmap: Tensor with an arbitrary complex (proof lines 14263-14270).
Check degreewise exactness by flatness (proof lines 14270-14278).
Use two out of three for acyclicity and conclude (proof lines 14278-14281).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the two-out-of-three property for K-flat complexes in a short exact sequence, under the additional hypothesis that the third complex is flat in every degree, and the proof is a 19-line argument that tensors the sequence with an arbitrary complex and inspects the resulting sequence of total complexes. The exactness of that sequence is checked degreewise, where the degreewise exactness follows from the flatness hypothesis through the vanishing of Tor, and then the conclusion is reduced to the elementary fact that in a short exact sequence of complexes acyclicity also satisfies two out of three. Both the degreewise reduction and the final step are displayed.
